disclaimer: OBSERVED claims only. Primary preferred. Secondary labeled. Generation interconnection data are not load-interconnection data. Backlog growth is demand evidence, not by itself a measured shortage. 2028–2030 capacity is not 2026 capacity.

source_inventory.title: Siemens Energy Earnings Release Q3 FY 2026
Microsoft FY2026 Q1 Earnings Conference Call
POWER Magazine on Wood Mackenzie Q2 2025 transformer survey
Utility Dive: GE Vernova 116 GW backlog and DC share
Data Center Knowledge citing PJM post-ISA delays

claims.subject: large-power-transformers
claims.statement: Siemens Energy Grid Technologies: Q3 FY2026 orders rose across all GT businesses; the major contribution was substantial growth in the transformer business including data center projects; book-to-bill 1.48; order backlog increased to €51bn.
claims.source_title: Siemens Energy Earnings Release Q3 FY 2026
claims.notes: Backlog and book-to-bill >1 are demand/queue evidence. They do not by themselves quantify weeks of lead time.

claims.subject: large-power-transformers
claims.statement: Siemens Energy plans transformer and gas-insulated switchgear manufacturing capacity about 50% higher by 2030; brownfield expansions supported increased product shipments in the reported quarter, with further greenfield/brownfield additions through FY30.
claims.source_title: Siemens Energy Earnings Release Q3 FY 2026
claims.notes: 2030 capacity is not 2026 capacity. Score as capacity_growth, not current relief.

claims.subject: large-power-transformers
claims.statement: GAO (2023): utilities identified supply-chain constraints as the most pressing LPT challenge; one large utility reported LPT lead times rising from 12–18 months to 18–36 months; smaller utilities reported worse delays.
claims.notes: Dated 2023 primary. Establishes structural LPT lead-time lengthening; not a 2026 week measurement.

claims.subject: large-power-transformers
claims.statement: Secondary reporting of Wood Mackenzie Q2 2025 survey: power transformers averaging 128 weeks; generator step-up transformers 144 weeks; GSU demand +274% and substation power transformers +116% since 2019.
claims.notes: Not used as sole scarcity proof. Confirms direction of 2023 GAO finding; week-level figures are secondary.

claims.subject: electrical-switchgear
claims.statement: GE Vernova: data center orders in Electrification reached over $5 billion year-to-date, more than double the 2025 total.
claims.notes: Electrification (grid/electrical equipment), not Gas Power turbines. Demand evidence for DC electrical gear.

claims.subject: gas-turbines
claims.statement: GE Vernova Q2 2026: Gas Power equipment backlog and slot reservation agreements grew from 100 to 116 GW; company anticipates at least 125 GW by year-end 2026; on track for 20 GW annual gas turbine output in Q3 2026, 24 GW in 2028, and actions to produce 30 GW in 2030.
claims.notes: 116 GW vs ~20 GW/year is quantified scarcity for heavy-duty turbines. 2028/2030 output is not current capacity. Mix is not all datacenter.

claims.subject: gas-turbines
claims.statement: Secondary report of GE Vernova earnings commentary: about 20% of the gas-power order book is data-center / AI applications and 80% traditional customers; CEO taking reservations for 2031 deliveries.
claims.source_title: Utility Dive on GE Vernova Q2 call
claims.notes: Used to avoid treating the entire 116 GW book as an AI-datacenter shortage.

claims.subject: grid-interconnection
claims.statement: LBNL Queued Up 2026: as of end-2025, ~8,244 active U.S. projects seeking transmission interconnection, ~2,061 GW (1,312 GW generation and 749 GW storage).
claims.notes: This is generation/storage interconnection, not datacenter load interconnection.

claims.subject: grid-interconnection
claims.statement: LBNL: for regions with data, median duration from interconnection request to commercial operation was over 5 years for projects built in 2025.
claims.notes: Time-to-COD includes post-ISA construction, not only study-queue time.

claims.subject: transmission-substations
claims.statement: LBNL: 549 GW of capacity already has a draft or executed interconnection agreement but has not reached commercial operations (including 45 GW of gas).
claims.notes: Shows post-agreement delivery is a distinct constraint from getting into the study queue.

claims.subject: utility-generation-headroom
claims.statement: PJM 2026 long-term load forecast: RTO summer peak growth averaging 3.6%/year over 10 years; summer peak 222,106 MW in 2036 (+65,733 MW) and 253,077 MW in 2046. Multiple zones adjusted for data-center load.
claims.notes: Forecasted demand, not a measured present reserve-margin breach. Near-term peaks were revised down vs 2025 forecast after vetting large-load requests.

claims.subject: utility-generation-headroom
claims.statement: PJM Inside Lines: 10-year average annual growth is 3.6%/year versus 0.3%/year in the 2021 forecast; near-term peaks through 2032 are lower than the 2025 forecast after improved vetting of data-center and large-load requests.
claims.source_title: PJM Inside Lines on 2026 load forecast
claims.notes: Do not treat every announced data-center MW as certain load.

claims.subject: ai-accelerators
claims.statement: Microsoft CFO on FY2026 Q1 call: the company was not actually short GPUs and CPUs per se; it was short the space or the power to put them in; remaining short for many quarters as demand increased.
claims.notes: Directly falsifies chips-as-#1 for this datacenter-expansion question, for this hyperscaler at this date.

claims.subject: datacenter-shells
claims.statement: Same Microsoft FY2026 Q1 commentary: constraint language is space or power to install compute, with continued build-out and increased use of leases (15–20 year assets).
claims.notes: Space is observed as a co-stated constraint with power; does not prove construction labor/materials are the scarce input versus energized halls.

claims.subject: electrical-switchgear
claims.statement: Eaton Q1 2026 analyst presentation: Electrical Americas data center orders up approximately 240% and revenue up approximately 50% versus 1Q25; Electrical Americas backlog up 44% year-over-year; book-to-bill 1.2 on a rolling 12-month basis.
claims.notes: Order surge is demand. Revenue +50% shows they are also shipping more — do not equate orders with inability to supply.

claims.subject: electrical-switchgear
claims.statement: Eaton Q2 2026: Electrical Americas record $4.0B sales, +18% organic; 12-month rolling orders +41% organically; Electrical Americas backlog +33% versus June 2025; electrical businesses book-to-bill 1.2.
claims.notes: Sustained book-to-bill above 1.0 indicates backlog still growing, not a measured multi-year LPT-class lead time.

claims.subject: liquid-cooling
claims.statement: Vertiv Q2 2026: organic sales growth with AI and general compute demand intensifying; Q2 revenue had minor timing shifts from temporary supply-chain congestion and multi-phased project execution; company raised full-year sales guidance and is accelerating capacity expansion.
claims.notes: Congestion is observed but described as temporary; raising guidance argues against treating cooling as the binding system constraint.

claims.subject: permitting-siting
claims.statement: Secondary report citing PJM January 2026 presentation: permitting accounted for 29% of milestone change requests for projects under construction or development, ahead of supply-chain delays at 23%.
claims.source_title: Data Center Knowledge citing PJM milestone data
claims.notes: Not independently retrieved from a PJM PDF in this build. Permitting is a delay cause, not proven as the highest-scarcity node.

claims.subject: transmission-substations
claims.statement: Secondary report citing PJM: projects entering service in 2025 averaged more than seven years to operation, with more than three years to an interconnection service agreement and another four years after approval; transformer lead times cited as exceeding 160 weeks in 2026.
claims.notes: Used only as triangulation that post-ISA time can exceed study time. 160-week transformer figure is not treated as primary.

claims.subject: gas-turbines
claims.statement: Siemens Energy Gas Services shipped 6 GW and booked 15 GW in the quarter ending 30 June 2026; company commentary (via secondary) puts gas-services backlog near 69 GW with turbine lead times of three years or more.
claims.source_title: Siemens Energy Q3 FY2026 (primary orders/revenue; backlog mix in release)
claims.notes: Primary PDF confirms GT/GS order strength and group backlog €162bn. Specific 69 GW / 3-year lead time is widely reported from the same quarter's analyst materials; do not over-precise beyond the earnings release text.
